title: Every time the panel opens, it downloads the gym's whole history again in one piece
what: When the panel is opened or reloaded, it asks the server for every record the gym has ever had (all members, plans, receipts and every check-in) in a single answer, even though this device already keeps a saved copy with a version number it could catch up from. For a gym with 500+ members and a year or two of daily check-ins that is tens of thousands of records on every open, over slow 4G, and one very large server answer that can run into the server's time limit. Each open also writes a 'pulled the whole copy' line to the gym's access log.
expected: The panel opens from the copy it already has and asks only for what changed since then; a full download happens only on a new device.
who: owners and desk staff of bigger gyms
how_often: every time the panel is opened or reloaded
fix_line: Start from the saved copy on the device and fetch only newer records; split a first full download into pages.

title: Each save and each change from another desk rebuilds and copies the whole gym
what: Every single action at the desk (a check-in, a payment, an edit) turns the whole gym, all members and every past check-in and receipt, into text, reads it back into a scratch copy, then compares every record one by one to find what changed. Every 15 seconds, when another desk or the entry machine saved something, the panel again sorts and copies the whole gym for the screens and writes the whole gym to the device's saved copy. On a 500+ member gym with long history on a cheap desk phone or old PC, taps get slower as the gym gets older.
expected: A save works only on the records it touches, and a change from another desk updates only those records on screen and in the saved copy.
who: desk staff of bigger, older gyms
how_often: every save, and every 15 seconds while another desk is busy
fix_line: Change and compare only the records an action touches, and update the saved copy by record instead of rewriting all of it.

title: A gym kept in this browser only fills the browser's space within months of daily check-ins
what: A gym that never signed in keeps everything in one block of the browser's small storage (about 5 MB). The code's own note sizes this for members and payments, but every check-in is a record too: a gym of a few hundred members checking in most days fills it in a few months. From then on every save, including each check-in, is refused with 'This browser is full'. Each check-in also rewrites the whole block, so saves slow down as it grows.
expected: The panel warns well before the space runs out and moves the owner to an online gym, or keeps check-ins in the larger device store.
who: owners using a gym kept only in the browser
how_often: once the gym has a few months of check-ins
fix_line: Warn as the space fills (for example at 70 percent) and point to putting the gym online, or move the browser-only gym to the larger device store.

title: The sign-in screen waits for the whole panel to download first
what: The sign-in, new-gym and Forgot PIN screens are part of the panel's one big download; only the Excel tools are fetched later. On a first visit over slow 4G the owner sees nothing to type into until every screen of the panel has arrived. The panel itself was not in the speed test run, so the real wait is not measured.
expected: The sign-in screen arrives first and small, and the rest of the panel loads while the person types.
who: new owners and staff on a first visit
how_often: every first visit and after each update
fix_line: Load the panel's screens in parts so sign-in shows first; add the panel's sign-in page to the speed test.

title: The terms-acceptance list has no index for who accepted
what: The list of who accepted the MettleUp terms links to the person who accepted, but that link has no index, so removing a person from the panel checks the whole list. The list is small today, so the cost is tiny.
expected: Every link between tables has an index.
how_often: each time a person is removed
fix_line: Add an index on the person column of the terms-acceptance list.
